answer_1.quote: We first use the MT-Bench dataset to assess the ability of different LLMs to compare two model-generated answers to a user-question in a chatbot interaction: a common task in LLM post-training...
answer_1.outputs: pairwise preference judgments, Likert-scale scores, probe-based classification outputs

answer_2.quote: We also report a recent improvement to this approach, G-Eval, which re-weights predictions using the model's own predicted probabilities for each possible answer choice...

answer_3.quote: Both supervised and unsupervised probes perform similarly to each other at aligning with this ground-truth... Importantly, we find probes outperform prompting, while maintaining the same inference cost of two forward passes per example...

answer_4.quote: A panel of human judges reached 80% agreement on this dataset, and we obtain ground-truth labels by taking the majority-vote of this panel...
answer_4.guideline: Human raters judged which of two model answers was preferred, using criteria such as helpfulness, relevance, and overall quality.
